title: Cornetists Tig Chambers and Joe Howard
summary: Morris does not know Ned or Joe Johnson, but recalls Tig Chambers with Dusen and Joe Howard, a fine cornetist who later played tuba.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Do you remember a cornet player by the name of Ned? They called him Ned. I don't know if it was his first or last name.
Ned. Ned. Ned, no, no. I'm trying to think of him now. No, I don't remember Ned.
What was, who'd he play with and what'd he play like?
Tig Chambers used to play with, wait, wait, wait. I'm going to tell you who Tig. Tig Chambers used to play with Frankie Dewson, too.
Yeah. Tig Chambers used to play with Frankie Dewson.
Was he good on blues or was he good?
Oh, yeah, he was a big, heavy softball. Yeah, Tig Chambers used to play with Frankie Dewson.
Did he have any special numbers?
No, well, I couldn't realize the special numbers, but I know, I'll tell you that much of it anyhow. Yeah.
You remember Joe Johnson. What was he like?
No, Joe Johnson. What did he used to play?
Joe Johnson, Joe Johnson. No, I remember Joe Howard. Do you remember him? Yeah. He used to play cornette now. I used to play with him, too.
He played tuba in the late...

That's right. When he died, he was playing tuba. Yes, sir. I used to play with him. He was a good cornette player, too. Yes, sir. He was what you call a real musician. Anything you put for him, he could hit.
